name: payment-bkash
description: A payment provider on bKash Tokenized Checkout: a hosted bKash page, settled by a status re-read, with refunds. Needs a bKash merchant account.

envVars.BKASH_APP_KEY: The app key of your bKash merchant account, from https://developer.bka.sh for the sandbox and from bKash's merchant onboarding for live. Read from apps/api/.env in local dev (saasaloy env, then pnpm env:setup) and from a Workers secret in production. Unset, every bkash call throws PaymentError("invalid_request") naming this key before anything is sent.
envVars.BKASH_APP_SECRET: The app secret issued with the app key. It is sent on the token grant and the token refresh, so a deployed Worker holds it as a secret (`wrangler secret put BKASH_APP_SECRET`), never in wrangler.jsonc.
envVars.BKASH_USERNAME: The merchant API username, sent as the `username` header on the two token calls. It is not your bKash wallet number and not your portal login.
envVars.BKASH_PASSWORD: The merchant API password that goes with the username, sent as the `password` header on the two token calls. A Worker secret for the same reason the app secret is.
envVars.BKASH_MODE: Which gateway host to use: `live` for https://tokenized.pay.bka.sh, anything else for the sandbox at https://tokenized.sandbox.bka.sh. Optional, and it fails safe: only the exact string `live` selects the live gateway, so a typo sends a test payment to the sandbox.

removeWarnings: Removing this module does not refund or cancel anything at bKash. Settle open bkash payments in the bKash merchant portal first; a payment row that names provider "bkash" can no longer be refunded from the admin page.
The stored gateway token stays in your kv store under the `payment:bkash:token` key until it expires. Delete it if you are rotating the app key.
If you handed bKash support a webhook listener URL during onboarding, ask them to remove it. Otherwise bKash keeps posting to an endpoint that now answers 404.

`@repo/kv` stays in packages/payment/package.json and `@repo/payment` stays in packages/queue/package.json, as every package-json-dependency patch does. Drop them with `pnpm remove` once nothing imports them.
